title: He Was Clinically Blind on One Side, Yet Pointed to Lights 90% Right
description:
Behavioral & Circuit Analysis — Lawrence Weiskrantz (1974): 'Blindsight' — Patient D.B. Pointing With 90% Accuracy Into Total Conscious Darkness, grounded in L. Weiskrantz, Elizabeth K. Warrington, M. D. Sanders, J. Marshall (1974) (Brain). Empirical findings show that standard neurology before 1974 taught a simple rule: destroy human primary visual cortex (V1 at the back of the occipital lobe), and the opposite half of space goes permanently, 100% blind — because physicians only ever asked 'Tell me when you SEE the light'.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how primary visual cortex, optic nerve, parietal cortex coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that inspired by Nicholas Humphrey's monkey 'Helen' (who caught moving currants without V1), Elizabeth Warrington and Lawrence Weiskrantz tested Patient D.B. at Queen Square in 1973-1974 after surgical removal of his right V1 left his left visual field completely blind on standard hospital perimetry.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- L. Weiskrantz, Elizabeth K. Warrington, M. D. Sanders, J. Marshall (1974). VISUAL CAPACITY IN THE HEMIANOPIC FIELD FOLLOWING A RESTRICTED OCCIPITAL ABLATION. Brain. https://doi.org/10.1093/brain/97.1.709
- Lawrence Weiskrantz (1992). UNCONSCIOUS VISION. The Sciences. https://doi.org/10.1002/j.2326-1951.1992.tb02415.x
- M. Jeannerod (1988). Blindsight. A case study and implicationsL. Weiskrantz. Oxford Psychology Series, No. 12, Clarendon Press, Oxford, 1986. Neuropsychologia. https://doi.org/10.1016/0028-3932(88)90017-6
